_comment: dossiq's capability matrix, at the path every product's matrix uses, and the only copy: the Features & roadmap page imports it from here. Ids, capability texts and ratings are RE-ISSUED FROM THE CORPUS by scripts/sync-capability-comparison.mjs. Do not edit those by hand: the corpus is ConductionNL/market-intelligence, procest/_ledger/parity-ledger.html, and every id, capability text and rating here comes from it. What is authored here and carried through a re-issue: per row `provider`, `providerHow`, `feature`, `featureConfidence`, `built` (the machine-readable half of a closure: prose saying closed is not a closed row) and `evidence` (what was seen, per system), and per system `evidenceGrade` and `unknownReason`. A hand edit to the ratings is what happened on 2026-09-10, and it put 104 rows on this page that no corpus artefact held, under ids the corpus used for other questions. tests/vitest/capabilityComparison.spec.js now fails when the id set here differs from capabilityComparison.corpus-ids.json. `capabilities` are the 225 ROWS: every column has been read against each of them, and `comparedOn` is the date the first four were read. It moves only when all four are read again. A column added later carries its own `readOn` and `columnAddedOn`, because moving `comparedOn` to cover it would make the reading-date sentence false for the four it already covers. A row added by a later round carries its own `addedOn` and rates every competitor `unknown`, because a guess in someone else's column is worse than an empty cell, and `rowsAddedOn` is the most recent of those dates. `pending` are the 146 PROPOSALS: questions raised against one product, not yet read against the rest. Every competitor cell on them is `unknown` and our own is rated, because we can always read our own code. They are not rows and they are not counted in any tally. A proposal becomes a row when every column has been read for it, and its id is assigned at that moment, centrally, in the corpus. Our OWN column is corrected between rounds, because a rating that says we lack something we shipped is the one error on this page a reader cannot check for themselves. The competitor columns are NOT corrected that way: we would be re-reading someone else's product without saying so, and the honest fix for those is a new round with a new comparedOn. Every correction and every added row is in `_rerated` with its date and its reason, and `reratedOn` carries the latest.

Case types group into folders by category. Attributes and templates do not, so this is partial and not yes.
Round 3 row. Two reports of the same nuisance on two channels is routine front-office work. We relate cases, we never collapse them, and a late reply to the closed one reaches nobody.
Round 3 row. Nothing on our intake path looks for a case that already exists.
Round 3 row, narrowed. The proposal also asked whether the pause reason is stored, which row 2.11 already asks. What is left is the chasing, and nothing in the app re-asks.

Round 3 row. CaseRelationService types a link as vervolg, subject or bijdrage and writes it on both cases, but the mirror carries the same name, so no link means blocks on one side and blocked by on the other.
Round 3 row, refiled from access-and-privacy to case-core: a lock is concurrency, not access control. Two handlers can overwrite each other on a case and neither is told.
Round 3 row. Our bulk actions each do one thing, and none of them decides where the handler lands afterwards.
Round 3 row. One flag per entry is what makes a single timeline safe to show an applicant. Row 6.4 is already no for the timeline, so the flag was never in question.
Round 3 row, refiled from integrations to communication. We score no and we are content with it: a municipality owes an applicant an outcome, not a rating request.
Round 3 row. Article 1 of the Algemene termijnenwet extends a term that ends on a Saturday, Sunday or recognised holiday. We add the days and stop.

Round 3 row. Round 3 read five private calendars and rated us no. WorkingDayCalculator has since landed and all five callers use it, so the single source of truth exists. Nobody can edit a holiday without a release, so this is partial and not yes.
Round 3 row, and one we lead on. DeadlinePauseService moves the end date out and pulls back the unused part when the applicant answers early, which is what Awb 4:15 asks for.

Round 3 row. DeadlineEscalationService widens from handler to teamleader to manager at 14, 7, 2 and 0 days. The ladder is a constant in code and not yet administered, which is a refinement rather than a gap.
Round 3 row. TermijnService stores both end dates as a date. A Dutch term expires at the close of a day, so storing a timestamp would be wrong here.
Round 3 row. Our threshold alerts sit on complaint analytics, not on a saved search.

Round 3 row. Round 3 rated us no and missed the Hours booked tile, which now books hours and runs a timer against the case. The hours live in humaniq and there is no rate or cost model, so this is partial and not yes.
Round 3 row. We hide actions and widgets on a field value, and field permissions exist per role, but no rule combines the two and none of it makes a field mandatory.
Round 3 row. Answers reused across cases are most of what a contact centre does, and we have no place to keep them.
Round 3 row. Row 13.12 covers mandates and deputies as a delegation of rights. This asks whether a case assigned to someone on leave shows up on anybody's list, and it does not.
Round 3 row. A favourite is navigation and row 2.19 already asks about it. A watch is a subscription, and a jurist following a sensitive case has no way to ask for one.

Merge into is a header action on the case (`src/manifest.json:3367`) opening `CaseMergeDialog`, where the surviving case is searched for and a reason is required. `CaseMergeService` asks OpenRegister to merge (`ObjectsMergedEvent`), `CaseMergedListener` moves the declared rows and completes the merged case's term, a reply quoting the old number reaches the survivor, and the merge can be reversed for seven days. Every `new-case` open-form carries `createOverride: caseCreateWithDuplicateCheck` (`src/manifest.json:641,1141,6921,7213`), which asks OpenRegister's `dedup-check` before the case is written and names the matches. Shipped by dossiq#2900.

A case type declares `pauseReasons`, each with a reminder interval, a count and an escalation target. A pause arms one reminder per rung on the term's timer and `PauseChaseJob` (registered in `appinfo/info.xml:175`) sweeps as well, both through `PauseChaseService::chaseIfDue()`, which sends by the route the request left by, records it on the term and the timeline, and escalates after the last one. The case page is a manifest detail page, and `CnDetailPage` in nextcloud-vue 2.57.0 (dossiq requires ^2.57.0) takes OpenRegister's lock when the edit form opens, releases it on save or close, names the holder in `CnLockedBanner` and withdraws Edit while someone else holds it. dossiq pins the register and schema the lock url is built from (`src/manifest.json:3187`). OpenRegister queues text extraction for every file written into an object folder, a case folder included (`FileChangeListener`, registered at `lib/AppInfo/Application.php:2928`, scope `objects` and mode `background` by default), and chunks the text. Nextcloud's search bar reads those chunks and answers with the owning case (`lib/Search/ObjectsProvider.php:519`, `_content_search`), and the case schema is searchable. The index is keyword over chunks in the database, with no external engine. openregister's own matrix (openregister#4040, row `srch-file-content`) reads this as API only with no screen; that misses `ObjectsProvider.php:519`, because Nextcloud's search bar is a screen and it searches file text.

Every case timeline entry has a side: the note composer and the Log contact action ask Visible to the applicant (`contactmoment.visibleToApplicant`, `src/manifest.json:3276`), outgoing messages and a sent beschikking are public by construction, and a status move is public when its status carries a `publicLabel`. `ContactMomentTimelineListener` writes every logged contact, and the public status page shows the applicant only the public entries. Shipped by dossiq#2907.

A term's end date is counted and rolled in one call: `TermEndRoll` moves an end that falls on a weekend or public holiday to the next ordinary day on the organisation calendar, falling back to a local working day calendar when the engine has none. `deadlineDefinition.rollToWorkingDay` defaults to on (`lib/Settings/register.d/60-termijnbewaking.json:66`) and switches it off for a term the Awt does not govern, and the admin terms tab shows the roll. Shipped by dossiq#2941.

Nextcloud's search bar finds a case by a word inside one of its documents, through OpenRegister's extracted file text (`lib/Search/ObjectsProvider.php:519`, `_content_search`). Held at partial: the hit is the case and not the document (openregister `content-search-index` task 1.1 is open), and dossiq's own Cases search does not search document content.

OpenRegister keeps an exports area where each prepared export carries an expiry, a download count and a status, swept when it expires (`lib/Db/ExportRun.php`, `GET /api/exports` at `appinfo/routes.php:1937`, `SweepExpiredExportRunsJob`). Follow is a strip on the case page (`CaseFollowStrip` in `CaseBannerStack`, placed as `case-banner-stack` at `src/manifest.json:2922`) over OpenRegister's `PUT|DELETE .../watch`. Followed cases are a lens on the Cases list, the People tab lists the followers (`case-followers`, `src/manifest.json:2534`), and the case schema notifies its watchers when the case moves. pending.dossiqNote: Rated from the source: `archiefstatus` is ZGW data on the zaak, defaulting to `nog_te_archiveren` (`lib/Service/ZgwZrcRulesService.php:121`) and guarded on delete (`lib/Controller/ZrcController.php:1265`, *Archived zaken cannot be deleted without the zaken.geforceerd-verwijderen scope.*). Nothing hides an archived zaak from a list or makes it read-only: the status is a fact about the archive, not a state of the working view. OTOBO and Znuny drove `ticket.archive_flag` in batch 5 and Odoo `action_archive` in batch 6; Jira DC documents "hide it in Jira, but preserve the data it contains", Data Center only, with archive and restore as automation triggers. Easy Redmine is `partial`: a project is archived and "almost completely hidden", a single ticket is closed or deleted. Not 4.20, an export in an archival format, and not 8.7, a destruction date.

pending.name: Does every write path to a date field agree, and does the product show one date for that field.
pending.dossiqNote: Rated from the source, and this is the row that indicts us. **Nine controllers** can set a date on a case: `TermijnController`, `DeadlineReportingController`, `ZrcController`, `DwangsomController`, `ComplaintController`, `ConsultationController`, `AdviceController`, `WOOAssessmentController` and `ContactMomentController`. Ten services carry a deadline in their name, beside `WorkingDayCalculator` and `SlaCalculator`. The only normaliser in the tree is **private**, `normaliseDate()` at `lib/Service/Doorlooptijd/CaseEnricher.php:252`, reachable by one caller. Nothing asserts that the nine writers agree and no test compares them. Gitea is the proof that a correct end-of-day rule, a correct administered time zone and a correct implementation of both, on one of three paths, still shows a caseworker the wrong day. Taiga passes by declining the question: `due_date` is a `DateField`, so there is no time of day and no zone. For dossiq this is an audit instruction before it is a competitive row, and it has been opened as change `one-date-write-path` in dossiq#2697. Batch 12 asks for it to be widened before promotion: Tuleap's write paths agree perfectly and its **read** paths differ by a calendar day on the screen the caseworker uses.

pending.name: Can an administrator define a role and choose its permissions, or only assign a role the product ships.
pending.dossiqNote: Rated from the source. A role type is an **object in a register**, not a constant: `lib/Service/WorkflowStepAuthorizationResolver.php:164-171` resolves `role_type_schema` from settings and looks the role type up through `ObjectService::find()`, and `VthCaseTypeChildSeeder.php:75` seeds `roleTypes` against it. `RoleResolverService` resolves a case's participants against those types with a named strategy (`STRATEGY_SINGLE_ROLE`, `STRATEGY_OR_SET`, `lib/Service/RoleResolverService.php:55-60`). An administrator creates a role type the way they create anything else. The row exists because 13.1, are there application roles, returns `yes` for every system in the corpus with any concept of a role and therefore separates nothing; the question a municipality asks is whether *behandelaar*, *toetser* and *mandaathouder* can exist without a release. Taiga defines roles per project with permissions ticked from a list of 33, verified live; Gitea and Forgejo score `no` on a fixed ladder of read, write and admin, where a team refines which units it holds rather than what a role means.

pending.name: Does the product offer the same configuration vocabulary whichever mode you configure it in, and does it say what you lose.
pending.dossiqNote: A `yes` by absence, and the row is worth carrying for exactly that reason. dossiq has one case-type editor and one configuration surface, so there is no second mode to lose capability in. The shape the row catches is general and we are about to acquire it: any product that grows a basic and an advanced surface over the same objects can strand a buyer between them. Tuleap is the reason the row exists and scores `partial`: the tracker workflow has a simple and an advanced mode, advanced mode makes the transition matrix explicit and **refuses two of the four post actions**, `frozen_fields` and `hidden_fieldsets` both throwing `IncompatibleWorkflowModeException` when `$workflow->isAdvanced()` (`FrozenFieldsJsonParser.php:46`, `HiddenFieldsetsJsonParser.php:47`). Driven: the same `PUT` refused in advanced mode succeeded in simple mode, and the per-transition permissions worked in both. So Tuleap does say what you lose, clearly and by name, at the moment you try, and does not say it when you switch modes, which is when it matters. Huly is `no`: one process editor per master tag, no second mode, and nothing anywhere warns about the consequence of a configuration choice. Rows 11.20 and 11.1 cannot ask this, because neither notices that a product can have two editors over the same objects with different capabilities.

pending.name: When an administrator defines a role, where do its permissions come from, and can a right be removed as well as granted.
pending.dossiqNote: **Unmeasured, and marked so deliberately.** Unlike 8.23 this needs the permission resolver read end to end rather than a grep, and batch 12 had two systems to drive. The interesting half is not whether a role can be defined, which 13.24 already asks and dossiq passes, but whether a right can be taken away: if dossiq's model is additive only, so that a role grants and never removes, this is a `partial` and a real gap. Huly is `yes` and it is the best answer in the corpus: a role is defined on a **master tag**, so roles are per type rather than per application, the permissions it draws from are 52 declared named things rather than a grid (`CreateCardPermission`, `ApproveDocumentPermission`, `RunProcessPermission`, `GuestPermission` and the rest), and roughly a third have a **`Forbid` counterpart**, nine of them, so a role can remove a right the space would otherwise grant. Tuleap is `partial`: an administrator creates a user group per project and grants it anything, which is why 13.24 is `yes`, but the permission set is published nowhere a buyer can read, it is discovered screen by screen, the grants are per object rather than per role, and there is no negative permission.

pending.name: Is the calendar the deadline engine reads the same calendar the organisation administers.
pending.dossiqNote: Measured read-only over `procest/lib` rather than assumed. We have the calendar and it is the best in the corpus: `lib/Service/WorkingDayCalculator.php` administers the Dutch general holidays and **computes Easter itself** rather than calling PHP's `easter_date()`, with a comment explaining why, and nothing in twenty-six driven columns comes close. The row does not ask whether the calendar exists, it asks whether the engine reads it. **37 files do date arithmetic** and **5 reference `WorkingDayCalculator`**: `BackgroundJob/DsoDeadlineJob.php`, `Service/ComplaintService.php`, `Service/DsoCaseService.php`, `Service/Kcc/SlaCalculator.php` and the calculator itself. Thirty-two do not, and three of those are term paths by name: `Service/Beschikking/BezwaarTermijnScheduler.php:76` computes the bezwaar term as `->add(new DateInterval('P6W'))` from the bekendmaking date, `Service/NoticeOfDefaultService.php:171` computes the ingebrekestelling grace as `->modify('+N days')`, and `Service/DeadlinePauseService.php:93` credits a suspension back the same way. Six weeks from bekendmaking is the right term; extending it off a Saturday, a Sunday or a general holiday is what the Algemene termijnenwet requires and what the calculator is for, and these three do not call it. **This is an audit instruction and not a proven defect**: a file doing date arithmetic is not necessarily computing a statutory term, some of the thirty-two are report windows and seed data, and three of the thirty-two were read. What the count establishes is that the calendar is not on the critical path by construction. Huly is `no` and is the first system that could have passed: `PublicHoliday` is a real class with a date and a department and its own screen, and nothing outside HR reads it. Tuleap is `no` for the simpler reason that `opening_days` is a weekday mask with no holiday object at all. Promoted row 8.12 cannot distinguish "no calendar" from "a calendar the engine cannot see", which is a different and worse failure.

pending.name: Local change to a case type shipped as code, with the divergence detectable
pending.dossiqNote: Row 11.2 exports and imports case types. Nothing tracks that a municipality changed a published one, so an update either overwrites the local change or is never applied.
pending.name_nl: Lokale wijziging op een als code geleverd zaaktype, met zichtbaar verschil

pending.name: Field state driven by other field values, enforced on the API too
pending.dossiqNote: Row 11.25 hides and requires fields by role and case state. Nothing makes a field required because another field holds a particular value, and nothing enforces that on a write that skips the form.
pending.name_nl: Veldgedrag gestuurd door andere veldwaarden, ook afgedwongen op de API

pending.name: One rule set evaluated in the form and again on every API write
pending.dossiqNote: Resolved rather than assumed: StatusTransitionService re-evaluates the identical guard set on the POST transition path and throws GuardFailedException, so the rules do run server-side. It stays partial because the set is transition-scoped rather than per field on every write, and the board's drop handler bypasses it entirely.
pending.name_nl: Eén set regels beoordeeld in het formulier en bij elke API-schrijfactie

pending.name: Import as a durable record with an outcome per row
pending.dossiqNote: An import runs and reports at the end. Nothing survives it, so nobody can go back to a load from last month and see which rows failed and why.
pending.name_nl: Import als blijvend record met een uitkomst per regel

pending.name: One rule usable as a condition inside another
pending.dossiqNote: Row 11.20 rules stand alone. Without composition, the same condition is written out in twenty rules and corrected in nineteen of them.
pending.name_nl: Eén regel bruikbaar als voorwaarde binnen een andere regel

pending.name: Explanation written by an administrator on a status and on a transition
pending.dossiqNote: statusType.description exists and nothing renders it. There is no text on a transition at all, so the moment a handler is choosing is the moment with no guidance.
pending.name_nl: Toelichting van de beheerder bij een status en bij een overgang

pending.name: Alert when a nominated field's value already exists on another record
pending.dossiqNote: Nothing lets an administrator nominate a field as effectively unique and get a warning on save. A second case on the same KvK number is found later or never.
pending.name_nl: Melding als de waarde van een aangewezen veld al elders voorkomt

pending.name: Screen configuration stored as a patch, failing loudly when the layout moves
pending.dossiqNote: Rows 11.6 to 11.9 are all no, so there is no screen configuration to store yet. This is the mechanism to build them in, because the alternative drops a customer's change silently at the next release.
pending.name_nl: Scherminrichting bewaard als patch, die hoorbaar faalt bij een nieuwe indeling

pending.name: Automation condition on a before-state and an after-state, not only on now
pending.dossiqNote: Row 11.20 rules read current values, so moved into this status and is in this status are the same condition. The first fires once, the second fires every time anything is saved.
pending.name_nl: Automatiseringsvoorwaarde op de oude en de nieuwe waarde, niet alleen op nu

pending.name: Custom field added by an ordinary user, still searchable and groupable
pending.dossiqNote: Row 11.3 custom fields per case type is yes, and only an administrator can add one. A team that needs one field waits for a change request.
pending.name_nl: Eigen veld toegevoegd door een gewone gebruiker, nog steeds doorzoekbaar

pending.name: Published service catalogue whose leaf sets form, case type and term at once
pending.dossiqNote: Row 11.23 groups case types into folders for administrators. This is the citizen-facing side of the same object, and it is what makes a term resolvable per service rather than per case type.
pending.name_nl: Gepubliceerde dienstencatalogus waarvan een blad formulier, zaaktype en termijn zet

pending.name: Reference field whose choices are a query over the record being edited
pending.dossiqNote: Row 11.10 code lists are flat and fixed. A field cannot offer only the contacts of the organisation already chosen on this case.
pending.name_nl: Verwijsveld waarvan de keuzes een zoekvraag zijn op het record zelf

pending.name: Obsolete value removed from every picker without being deleted
pending.dossiqNote: workflowTemplate.lifecycleStatus carries deprecated, described as cannot back new cases while existing cases keep using it, and WorkflowDefinitionService enforces it and refuses a deprecation that would strand open cases. There is no equivalent for arbitrary code list values, and caseType.validUntil is shown but not enforced as a picker filter.
pending.name_nl: Vervallen waarde uit elke keuzelijst gehaald zonder te verwijderen

pending.name: Ledger of which rule fired for which case, and which actions succeeded
pending.dossiqNote: Rows 11.20 and 3.11 ask whether rules exist. Nothing records that one ran, so why did this case not get its letter has no answer short of reading the code.
pending.name_nl: Logboek van welke regel voor welke zaak liep en welke acties slaagden

pending.name: Rule conditions expressed relative to now, including in business hours
pending.dossiqNote: A rule cannot say created more than three working hours ago, so time-based escalation is written as jobs rather than as configuration a manager can change.
pending.name_nl: Regelvoorwaarden ten opzichte van nu, ook binnen openingstijden

pending.name: Named screen overrides bound to a team or a portal, with fall-through
pending.dossiqNote: Rows 11.6 to 11.9 are all no. One screen for handlers, a narrower one for the front office and a third for the portal is the ordinary requirement, and there is no shape for it.
pending.name_nl: Benoemde schermvarianten per team of portaal, met terugval op de basis

pending.name: Hierarchical code list whose entries carry consequences, not only labels
pending.dossiqNote: Row 11.10 is flat and each entry is a label. Nothing hangs a term, a route or a required document off the value the handler picks.
pending.name_nl: Hiërarchische keuzelijst waarvan de waarden gevolgen dragen, niet alleen labels

pending.name: Validation written by an administrator that refuses a save with its own message
pending.dossiqNote: FieldValidator and StepConfigValidator validate what the code says. An administrator cannot add a check, and cannot write the sentence the handler reads when it fails.
pending.name_nl: Validatie van de beheerder die opslaan weigert met een eigen melding

pending.name: Transition the person who prepared the case may not make themselves
pending.dossiqNote: Mandaat is modelled and MandaatVerifier reads it, and ConflictOfInterestService asks whether a handler is related to the applicant. No transition carries a negative flag, so nothing stops the person who wrote a decision from approving it.
pending.name_nl: Overgang die de voorbereider van de zaak niet zelf mag zetten

pending.name: Emergency self-granted access, time-boxed, with a reason, enabled per case type
pending.dossiqNote: Row 13.4 grants access, by somebody else, with no reason and no per-case-type switch. sociaalDomeinAuditLog.authorisationGround is declared in the register and has zero readers, so there is no time box, no reason and no access level per case type.
pending.name_nl: Noodtoegang die je jezelf geeft, tijdelijk, met reden, per zaaktype aan te zetten

pending.name: Hand-off refused until consent is recorded, with the sharing scope chosen
pending.dossiqNote: toestemming is declared in the sociaal domein register and the only toestemming hits in lib/ are Dutch error strings. CaseTransferService::initiateTransfer has no consent branch and createPartnerShare writes a share with no scope, so nothing is ever blocked.
pending.name_nl: Overdracht geweigerd tot toestemming is vastgelegd, met gekozen deelomvang

pending.name: Erasure for one person across every case, with a report of what was left
pending.dossiqNote: Rows 8.7 and 13.10 delete on a retention schedule. An erasure request names a person and has to reach identifiers inside message bodies and mail headers, and report honestly what it could not remove.
pending.name_nl: Wissen van één persoon over alle zaken, met een verslag van wat bleef

pending.name: Named role slot on the case, where the right follows whoever occupies it
pending.dossiqNote: Row 5.1 puts parties on a case with roles. Rights are granted to people and groups, not to the slot, so replacing the occupant means editing every grant.
pending.name_nl: Benoemde rolplek op de zaak, waarbij het recht meegaat met de bezetter

pending.name: Destruction proposed as a list, reviewed per item by a named reviewer
pending.dossiqNote: Rows 8.7 and 13.10 destroy on a date. A vernietigingslijst is reviewed item by item by a named reviewer and a co-reviewer, and each response is recorded before anything is destroyed.
pending.name_nl: Vernietiging voorgesteld als lijst, per stuk beoordeeld door een benoemde toetser

pending.name: Anonymising as a configured alternative to deletion, chosen per outcome
pending.dossiqNote: anonymisationAtParts has zero readers, and ArchivalNominationDeriver's whole action vocabulary is bewaren, blijvend_bewaren and vernietigen. There is no anonymise branch to configure.
pending.name_nl: Anonimiseren als ingerichte keuze naast verwijderen, per resultaat gekozen

pending.name: Report accepted without an account, unmasked only by a named custodian
pending.dossiqNote: The Wet bescherming klokkenluiders obliges a municipality to run exactly this surface. Nothing accepts a report against a receipt code, and nothing gates the reveal on a motivated request a custodian answers.
pending.name_nl: Melding zonder account aangenomen, alleen ontsloten door een benoemde vertrouwenspersoon

pending.name: Party relationship granting dated access to the other party's record
pending.dossiqNote: A gemachtigde, a guardian or a parent company should see the record they are entitled to see because of the relationship. Access is granted per case and per user instead.
pending.name_nl: Partijrelatie die gedateerde toegang geeft tot het record van de ander

pending.name: Tamper-evident audit log that can be verified after the fact
pending.dossiqNote: AuditPacketBuilder assembles the beschikking, its immutable transition log and a validation report into a ZIP and stamps it with a sha256 digest, routed at /api/beschikkingen/{id}/audit-pakket. It is a per-beschikking export, not a chained log over the whole trail, and no previousHash exists anywhere.
pending.name_nl: Auditlog waarin knoeien zichtbaar wordt en dat later te controleren is

pending.name: Link type declaring which fields of the linked record it exposes
pending.dossiqNote: Row 2.26 declares typed links. A link is all or nothing, so relating a Wmo case to a Jeugdwet case exposes everything or nothing rather than the two fields that were meant.
pending.name_nl: Koppelsoort die vastlegt welke velden van het gekoppelde record zichtbaar zijn

pending.name: Portal visibility derived from the party tree, so a parent sees its subsidiaries
pending.dossiqNote: Row 13.13 grants portal rights per case. A holding company with eleven subsidiaries is then eleven separate grants, maintained by hand as the group changes. Re-rated no to yes on 2026-09-26 from portaliq's code: portaliq lib/Service/Identity/PortalPartyTreeResolver.php:90-175 entitiesFor() walks the party tree; lib/Service/Identity/PortalMandateService.php:204-222 reachOf() returns REACH_TREE for a mandate that reaches down; lib/Controller/CitizenCaseController.php:693-696 applies it on the reached citizen-case path (portaliq matrix row sib-dossiq-13-38). Caveat from that portaliq row: the SPA never sends a mandate parameter, so the service's default mandate decides whether tree reach applies.
pending.name_nl: Portaalzicht afgeleid uit de partijboom, zodat een moeder de dochters ziet

pending.name: Notification when a file is downloaded
pending.dossiqNote: Row 13.9 logs a read. lib/Notification holds only the notifier and no download listener is registered, so nothing acts on one while it is happening.
pending.name_nl: Melding zodra een bestand wordt gedownload

pending.name: Permission to hand work to someone, distinct from read and write
pending.dossiqNote: The case schema says of the team that it is assignment, not permission. Reassignment is gated by a coordinator check that resolves to isAdmin, so handing work over is an admin right rather than an axis of its own beside read and write.
pending.name_nl: Recht om werk toe te wijzen, los van lezen en schrijven

pending.name: Row-level access by group, with the inheritance it came from declared
pending.dossiqNote: Rows 13.3 and 13.6 are both partial. Nothing says where a permission came from, and nothing marks one as not inheritable, so an access review cannot be finished.
pending.name_nl: Toegang per rij via groepen, met de herkomst van de overerving erbij

pending.name: Bearer link that opens a case without a login, with expiry and revocation
pending.dossiqNote: CaseSharingService::createTokenShare issues the link and revokeTokenShare withdraws it, both with an expiry. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
pending.name_nl: Deellink die een zaak opent zonder inloggen, met vervaldatum en intrekking

pending.name: Legal hold suspending destruction while a proceeding runs
pending.dossiqNote: LegalHoldApplier, BezwaarLegalHoldListener and AwbProceedingScanner place and lift the hold as a bezwaar or beroep opens and closes. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
pending.name_nl: Bewaarplicht die vernietiging opschort zolang een procedure loopt

pending.name: Bulk reassignment of a departing handler's caseload
pending.dossiqNote: CaseReassignmentService and SelectionReassignmentService move a whole caseload at once, by handler or by selection. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
pending.name_nl: Zaaklast van een vertrekkende behandelaar in bulk herverdelen

pending.name: Case plan of interventions, each with a goal, a provider and a target date
pending.dossiqNote: The register declares gezinsplan.goals and deploymentTrajectories as plain string arrays, with no provider, no target date and no completion mark, and nothing reads them. The schema cannot express the row, so this is no and not partial.
pending.name_nl: Plan van aanpak met interventies, elk met doel, aanbieder en streefdatum

pending.name: Award with amount requested, amount granted, payment, reporting and recovery
pending.dossiqNote: The Subsidie services carry the whole arc: award, interim reporting, final determination, evidence, co-financing and recovery, with the Dwangsom services beside them. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
pending.name_nl: Toekenning met gevraagd bedrag, verleend bedrag, betaling, verantwoording en terugvordering

pending.name: Offline field capture with a visible replay queue and recorded conflicts
pending.dossiqNote: dossiq registers the field-inspection leaf with its own offline config, and the leaf owns the queue and the replay. Its own Dexie store, sync queue engine, replay service and controller were deleted, so conflictRecord has no reader and an inspector still cannot work without a signal.
pending.name_nl: Offline opnemen in het veld met een zichtbare wachtrij en vastgelegde conflicten

pending.name: One instance serving several organisations, with separated data and quotas
pending.dossiqNote: Twenty Tenant services carry it, including TenantSchemaProvisioner, TenantQuotaService and TenantAuditTrailService. Added so the instrument can record a strength.
pending.name_nl: Eén omgeving voor meerdere organisaties, met gescheiden data en quota
